title: Platform systems & services: playbook, dashboards, runbooks, roadmap, and retro (Q3 2026 midyear)
author: Priya Desai
body:
Overview
========

This document is the central playbook for Platform Systems & Services (PSS) covering: architecture and owned services, dashboard and alert standards, operational runbooks for common incidents, practical how-tos for day-to-day ops, a brief retrospective of the biggest Q2 incident, and the Q3–Q4 2026 roadmap. It is intended for SREs, platform engineers, on-call responders, and product partners.

Scope
-----
- Systems covered: platform-api, ingest-proxy, routing-service, batcher, model-cache, telemetry-ingester, redwood-console, rbac-service
- Deploy targets: hosted (K8s/GKE), Dedicated GPU pools, Private (VPC) replicas
- Excluded: customer application services (see ownership matrix)

Ownership & Contacts
--------------------
- Platform SRE (primary on-call): @oncall-platform (Slack channel #oncall-platform)
- Service owners: platform-api (team: serving-runtime), batcher (team: infra), model-cache (team: serving-runtime), telemetry-ingester (team: eng-platform)
- Escalation: SRE Lead (Ethan Li), Platform Engineering Manager (Mariana Gomez)

Service SLAs / SLOs (production)
--------------------------------
- platform-api: availability 99.95% monthly, p95 latency < 200ms, p99 < 500ms for control-plane API (non-generation).
- routing-service: error rate < 0.3% sustained over 5m.
- batcher: throughput SLO 3x median request batching factor during peak.
- model-cache: KV cache hit ratio >= 90% for hot prefixes; miss storm detection when miss_rate > 10% for 10m.

Dashboards and Alerts (standards)
--------------------------------
All platform dashboards live in Grafana folder: "Platform / Services". Dashboards must include owner, critical panels, and runbook links. Standard panels: request rate (r/s), p50/p95/p99 latency, 5m error rate, CPU/GPU util, queue depth, batch size distribution, cache hit ratio, cost / token (daily).

Alerting policy (summary):
- Severity definitions:
  - Sev1 (page immediately): total system outage for >2 minutes or platform-api availability below 95% for 5m.
  - Sev2 (page and Slack): functional degradation (p99 > 1s or error rate > 1% for 10m).
  - Sev3 (Slack only): non-critical performance regressions or elevated error rates < 1% for 30m.

Base alert thresholds (examples):
- platform-api: error_rate > 0.5% for 5m -> Sev2.
- CPU utilization > 85% on control-plane nodes for 10m -> Sev3.
- GPU queue depth > 200 pending requests for 2m -> Sev1.
- KV cache miss_rate > 10% for 10m -> Sev2 and trigger cache-warm job.
- Datastore (Redis) latency p95 > 30ms for 5m -> Sev2.

Alert runbook links: panel >> runbook >> /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-playbook-runbooks-dashboards-roadmap-2026-q3-midyear.json#runbooks

Runbooks (common incidents)
--------------------------
1) platform-api high error rate / 5xx spike (Sev2)
Steps:
  1. Acknowledge the page (PagerDuty).
  2. Open Grafana "Platform / platform-api" -> check 1m/5m error rate and p95 latency.
  3. Check recent deploys: kubectl -n platform get deploy platform-api -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.metadata.annotations}' | jq .
  4. If deploy in last 30m, roll back: kubectl -n platform rollout undo deploy/platform-api --to-revision=<previous-revision>.
  5. Check ingress and certs: kubectl -n istio get virtualservices,gateways and cert-manager logs.
  6. Evaluate logs (ELK): 
     - Query: index=platform-logs service=platform-api level>=error | top 50 message
     - Look for 429s, auth errors, or dependency timeouts (redis/db).
  7. If dependency timeout -> triage downstream.
  8. Post incident summary to #oncall-postmortems within 24h.

2) GPU queue/backlog causing latency (Sev1)
Steps:
  1. Acknowledge page and gather initial metrics: GPU utilization, queue depth, batch size. Grafana panels: "GPU / queue depth", "Batcher / pending".
  2. Temporarily enable burst capacity (Dedicated) or scale up worker pool: kubectl -n inference scale deploy/batcher --replicas=<+2>.
  3. If queue persists, enable automatic model fallback routing: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/override -d '{"target_model":"small-quantized-v1","duration":"15m"}'
  4. If GPUs saturated due to a bad traffic pattern, apply rate limiting via the gateway: kubectl -n istio apply -f /manifests/rate-limit-temporary.yaml
  5. After stabilization, run a backlog drain validation and revert overrides.

3) KV cache miss storm (Sev2)
Steps:
  1. Confirm miss rate: Grafana "model-cache" cache_hit_ratio panel.
  2. If miss_rate > 10% for 10m, run manual warm-up: python tools/cache_warmup.py --prefixes-file=suspect_prefixes.txt --target=all-nodes --concurrency=8
  3. Increase TTL for hot keys: redis-cli -h <host> -a $REDIS_PASS EVAL "return 1" 0 (run via staging first).
  4. If Redis CPU/ops saturated, failover to read-replica and contact infra.

How-tos (common operator tasks)
-----------------------------
- Add a new Grafana panel:
  1. Fork the dashboard JSON in Grafana -> export -> update panels with appropriate PromQL.
  2. Add panel description: owner, alert link, runbook link.
  3. Commit JSON to infra/dashboards/platform and open PR against infra repo.
- Hotfix deploy to production (platform-api) without rollout:
  1. Build image and tag: IMAGE=registry.redwood/plat-api:$SHA
  2. kubectl -n platform set image deploy/platform-api platform-api=$IMAGE --record
  3. Monitor health: kubectl -n platform rollout status deploy/platform-api --timeout=5m
  4. If issues, rollback as per runbook above.
- Run a canary test for routing policy change:
  1. Create canary policy in control plane (JSON): set traffic percentage to 5% for 30m.
  2. Apply policy via curl to controlplane API and monitor canary dashboard.
  3. Promote to full traffic only after metrics confirm no regression.

Operational checks (daily)
------------------------
- Verify all Sev1 boards have no active alerts.
- Check platform-api p95 < 200ms.
- Confirm GPU pool spare capacity >= 15% for peak region.
- Run synthetic healthcheck: curl https://health.redwood.internal/platform-api/ready -> expect 200

Deck: Monitoring panels (quick reference)
---------------------------------------
| Panel name | Purpose | Owner | Alert linked |
|------------|---------|-------|--------------|
| platform-api requests | Traffic trends and spikes | serving-runtime | platform-api-error-rate |
| batcher queue | Backlog and batch sizes | infra | batcher-queue-depth |
| model-cache hit ratio | Cache efficiency | serving-runtime | cache-miss-storm |
| GPU utilization | Capacity planning | infra | gpu-saturation |

Retrospective: Q2 incident summary (May 2026)
-------------------------------------------
Incident: Intermittent platform degradation (12-14 May 2026) causing higher p99 latencies and elevated error rates for routing-service.
Root cause:
- NFS latency spikes on telemetry-ingester nodes during a nightly snapshot led to Redis eviction cascades in model-cache. This produced a cache miss storm and increased downstream load on model-serving batchers.
Contributing factors:
- Snapshot scheduled during peak backup window.
- Insufficient early-warning alerts for increasing Redis ops.
- Cache warm-up job ran only every 6h (too infrequent).
Actions taken (completed):
- Move NFS snapshots to off-peak window (COMPLETED 2026-05-20).
- Implemented Redis p95 latency alert (threshold 30ms) and throttle policy (COMPLETED 2026-05-22).
- Reduced cache warm-up interval to 30m and improved warm-up concurrency (COMPLETED 2026-06-01).
Planned (in-progress):
- Replace NFS-backed workspace with per-node ephemeral storage for telemetry-ingester (ETA Q4 2026).
- Add synthetic cache-miss drills to game-day schedule (ETA Q4 2026).

Roadmap (Q3-Q4 2026 priorities)
-------------------------------
1. Unified cost dashboard (Q3 2026) - per-route/per-model cost metrics integrated into Grafana. Owner: finance+infra.
2. Automated canary analysis (Q4 2026) - integrate A/B metrics and automated rollback for regressions. Owner: eng-platform.
3. Synthetic load harness (Q4 2026) - scheduled synthetic traffic with chaos tests for fallback paths. Owner: SRE.
4. Improved alerting: anomaly detection (Q3 2026) - experiment with ML-based anomaly alerts to reduce noise. Owner: telemetry team.
5. Private deployment runbook expansion (Q4 2026) - add VPC-specific diagnostics and on-prem packaging checklist. Owner: eng-private-deployments.

Team wiki & resources
---------------------
- Primary wiki index: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-team-wiki-runbooks-dashboards-roadmap-2026-q2.json
- Grafana folder: Grafana -> Platform / Services (contact: dashboards@redwood.internal)
- On-call rota and PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.redwood.internal/teams/platform
- Infra repo for dashboards: git@repo:redwood/infra-dashboards.git
- Tools: tools/cache_warmup.py, tools/canary_tester.py, scripts/rollout-rollback.sh

Appendix: Useful commands and snippets
------------------------------------
- Check platform-api recent errors (ELK):
  curl -s "https://elk.internal/api/search?q=service:platform-api+AND+level:error&size=50" | jq .
- Scale batcher replicas quickly:
  kubectl -n inference scale deploy/batcher --replicas=6
- Temporarily override routing to fallback model:
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/override \
    -d '{"target_model":"small-quantized-v1","duration":"15m"}'

Maintenance checklist for major releases
--------------------------------------
1. Update release notes and add dashboard panels for new metrics.
2. Schedule canary (5%) for 30m with automatic rollback condition.
3. Run pre-deploy smoke tests in staging.
4. Notify #platform-updates and product stakeholders.

Document maintenance
--------------------
- Owner: Priya Desai (eng-platform).
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any Sev1.
- To propose changes: open PR on infra-docs and add reviewer from SRE lead.

End of document.
